chapters.title: Chapter 3: TDS on Investment Income and Other Payments

lessons.title: Buying Property: The 1% TDS Rule and Form 26QB

body.text: Buy a property worth ₹50 lakh or more and you become a tax deductor. You must hold back 1% of the price, deposit it against your own PAN within weeks, and hand the seller a certificate. Miss it, and the interest and fees are yours to pay.

children.text: Kunal and Shreya, both software engineers in Pune, are buying a resale 2BHK in Baner from Mr Desai, a retired resident Indian, for ₹82,00,000. Between the home loan paperwork, stamp duty and the registration appointment, nobody mentions tax. But the moment they pay Mr Desai, the law makes them responsible for deducting TDS. This lesson walks through exactly what they must do, and what changes if the flat is under construction, jointly owned or sold by an NRI.

markDefs.definition: Land (other than agricultural land) or a building or part of a building, such as a flat, house, shop or office.

children.text: TDS on property purchases now sits in Section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, Table, Sl. No. 3(i) (formerly Section 194-IA). It applies to any buyer, including a salaried individual with no business, who pays a resident seller for

body.caption: TDS on buying property from a resident seller, tax year 2026-27

cells: The buyer, whether an individual, HUF, company or anyone else
When the price or the stamp duty value is ₹50,00,000 or more
1% of the higher of the price and the stamp duty value (20% if the seller has no valid PAN)
The whole amount, not just the part above ₹50,00,000
At each payment or credit to the seller, including advances and instalments
Form 141 (formerly Form 26QB), filed with your PAN within 30 days from the end of the month of deduction
Form 132 (formerly Form 16B), within 15 days from the Form 141 due date

markDefs.definition: The value of a property as fixed by the state government for charging stamp duty, often called the circle rate or ready reckoner rate. It can be higher than the price actually agreed.

children.text: Two details trip up buyers. First, the price includes charges that are part of the deal, such as car parking, club membership, electricity or water connection fees and maintenance charged by the seller. Second, TDS is calculated on the higher of that price and the
. Stamp duty and registration fees you pay to the state are not part of the price.

cells: Stamp duty value of the flat

body.title: Try It: How Much Reaches Mr Desai?
body.prompt: Kunal and Shreya pay the full price of ₹82,00,000 in one go at registration, after deducting TDS of 1% on the stamp duty value of ₹85,00,000. How much does Mr Desai actually receive?
body.explanation: TDS is 1% of the higher value, ₹85,00,000, which is ₹85,000. They pay ₹82,00,000 minus ₹85,000 = ₹81,15,000. The ₹85,000 is credited to Mr Desai's PAN, and he claims it against the capital gains tax on the sale.

body.title: Quick Check: Just Under ₹50 Lakh
body.question: Pooja agrees to buy a flat in Nashik for ₹48,00,000. The stamp duty value is ₹52,00,000. Does she need to deduct TDS?
options: No, because the price is below ₹50 lakh
Yes, but only on the ₹2 lakh by which stamp duty value exceeds ₹50 lakh
body.explanation: The exemption applies only when both the price and the stamp duty value are below ₹50,00,000. Here the stamp duty value crosses it, so TDS applies at 1% of the higher value, ₹52,000.

children.text: Since 1 October 2024, the ₹50,00,000 test looks at the total price of the property, not each buyer's or seller's share. Two siblings each paying ₹30,00,000 for a ₹60,00,000 flat must both deduct TDS. And each buyer deducts on their own share of the payment and files their own Form 141 with their own PAN.

If Mr Desai and his wife owned the flat jointly, each buyer would report both sellers and the share paid to each. Getting the split wrong is one of the most common reasons a seller's credit does not match.

events.title: Registration and payment
events.description: Each deducts ₹42,500 and pays the balance to Mr Desai.

events.title: Form 141 due
events.description: Each files Form 141 on the e-filing portal with their PAN, the seller's PAN and property details, and pays the TDS.

events.title: Form 132 due
events.description: Each downloads Form 132 from TRACES and gives it to Mr Desai.

events.title: Seller claims credit
events.description: Mr Desai sees ₹85,000 in Form 26AS and AIS and claims it in his return against tax on his capital gains.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Form
body.textWithBlank: From 1 April 2026, a buyer deposits TDS on a property purchase and reports it using Form ___, which replaced Form 26QB.
body.explanation: Form 141 is a single PAN-based challan-cum-statement for property purchases, rent paid by individuals, large contractor payments by individuals, and crypto transfers. It replaced Forms 26QB, 26QC, 26QD and 26QE.

children.text: Under-Construction Property: TDS on Every Instalment

For a flat bought from a builder on a construction-linked payment plan, TDS is deducted on each instalment as it is paid, and a separate Form 141 is filed for each one. Rhea, a doctor in Hyderabad, books a ₹1,20,00,000 flat payable in four stages.

body.title: TDS Rhea deducts at each stage

body.text: Home loans are where most buyers slip. Banks usually disburse the loan straight to the builder or seller, often for the full instalment. That does not move the TDS obligation to the bank. It stays with you. Either ask the bank to disburse 99% and pay the 1% yourself, or pay the TDS from your own funds and settle the difference with the seller.

children.text: The Cost of Getting It Wrong
Suppose Kunal deducts ₹42,500 on 15 December 2026 but only files Form 141 and deposits the tax on 20 March 2027, 49 days after the due date.

stats.label: Late filing fee
stats.context: ₹200 a day for 49 days, capped at the TDS amount

stats.label: Interest on late deposit
stats.context: 1.5% a month for 4 months under Section 398. Part of a month counts as a full month

stats.label: Total avoidable cost
stats.context: Paid by the buyer, not the seller

children.text: Had he not deducted at all, interest would run at 1% a month from the date of payment, he could be treated as an assessee in default for the tax itself, and penalties can follow. Meanwhile Mr Desai would find no credit in his Form 26AS, and sellers who are chasing a missing credit are rarely patient.

body.title: Scenario: The Seller Lives in Dubai
body.scenario: Arvind, a banker in Mumbai, is buying a ₹90,00,000 flat in Navi Mumbai from Mrs Iyer, who has lived and worked in Dubai for ten years and is a non-resident for tax. Arvind's broker tells him to "just deduct 1% like always".
body.prompt: Is the broker right? What should Arvind do?
body.modelAnswer: No. The 1% rule applies only when the seller is a resident. Payments to a non-resident fall under the table for non-residents in Section 393, where TDS is generally based on the capital gains tax the seller would owe, including surcharge and cess. That can be far higher than 1% of the price, and for a long-held property it is often worked out on the whole price unless the seller obtains a lower deduction certificate showing her actual gain. Arvind should ask Mrs Iyer whether she has, or will apply for, a lower or nil deduction certificate, and engage a chartered accountant before paying anything. Under the new PAN-based Form 141 system, buyers in such transactions reportedly no longer need a separate TAN, but the rate calculation is where the real risk lies. Deducting only 1% could leave Arvind liable for the shortfall, plus interest.

body.title: Before and After You Pay for a Property
steps: Confirm the seller is a resident and collect their PAN and Aadhaar-linked status before signing the agreement
Find the stamp duty value and compare it with the full price including parking, club and other charges
Agree in writing with the seller, and your bank if you have a loan, that 1% will be deducted from every payment
For each payment, file Form 141 with your PAN within 30 days from the end of that month
Download Form 132 from TRACES and give it to the seller within 15 days of the Form 141 due date
If there are co-buyers, make sure each files separately on their share, and all sellers are listed with correct shares

body.label: Income Tax e-Filing Portal: e-Pay Tax
body.description: Log in with your PAN and use the e-Pay Tax service to file Form 141 and pay TDS on a property purchase. Download Form 132 afterwards from TRACES.

cards.definition: TDS at 1% on buying immovable property from a resident when price or stamp duty value is ₹50 lakh or more. Formerly Section 194-IA.
The state-assessed value of a property for stamp duty. TDS is calculated on the higher of this and the price.
PAN-based challan-cum-statement for property TDS, due within 30 days from the end of the month of deduction. Formerly Form 26QB.
TDS certificate the buyer gives the seller, due within 15 days of the Form 141 due date. Formerly Form 16B.
Since 1 October 2024, the ₹50 lakh test applies to the total property price even with multiple buyers or sellers.
₹200 a day until the statement is filed, capped at the TDS amount. Formerly Section 234E.

points: Any buyer of property worth ₹50 lakh or more from a resident must deduct 1% TDS, under Section 393(1) Sl. No. 3(i), formerly 194-IA
TDS is on the higher of the full price (including parking, club and similar charges) and the stamp duty value, on the entire amount
Deposit and report with Form 141 using your PAN within 30 days from the end of the month, and issue Form 132 to the seller
Joint buyers each deduct and file on their share, and the ₹50 lakh test applies to the total price
For under-construction property, deduct on every instalment, and do not assume your bank handles TDS on loan disbursements
Buying from a non-resident is a different, far more expensive calculation, so get professional advice before paying

Provisions, form numbers and fees reflect the position understood at the time of writing and can change.
